selection.description: The prompt's selection when the parse was requested (`start === end` is the plain cursor position).

request_id.description: Reference number for this parse. Whatever answers it — the highlight echo (a prompt `configure` carrying `request_id`) — repeats it, so the machine can drop answers to superseded inputs (the user typed on in the meantime).

start.description: Inclusive starting position of the selection

end.description: Exclusive ending position of the selection

text.description: The prompt's text when the command fired (empty: fired elsewhere, see `anchor`).

selection.description: The prompt's selection when the command fired.

action.description: The action that fired: a key binding's, or a clicked part's.

id.description: Identifies this command. A driver that produces an echo in response repeats it as the echo's `id`, so the terminal can relate the two (e.g. to focus the new cell).

zone.description: Where what the command shows goes (a zone, as in `@zone cmd`), when the terminal decided it (e.g. a slot the user picked it for).

anchor.description: Where the command was performed, when not in the prompt: the address of the cell an inherited binding fired in (see `inherit` on actions). What the command shows is meant to go relative to it: pass it on as the `anchor` of what it configures.

Action.description: What a key binding, or a clicked part, does. The terminal only reads `freeze`, and sends the action to the driver (see CommandRequest), which carries it out. A string is a command line: short for `{command: <it>}`.

freeze.description: If true, the prompt's content is frozen as the action fires.

inherit.description: If true, the binding also works in every cell under the prompt's address (the cells of the commands run from it, and theirs...); the closest prompt's inherited binding for a key wins (and in a prompt, its own bindings). Fired from such a cell, the command request's `anchor` is that cell's address, and its text and selection are empty (not the prompt's).

CommandAction.description: A command line for the driver to run (as if submitted, but leaving the prompt and its history alone).

freeze.description: If true, the prompt's content is frozen as the action fires.

inherit.description: If true, the binding also works in every cell under the prompt's address (the cells of the commands run from it, and theirs...); the closest prompt's inherited binding for a key wins (and in a prompt, its own bindings). Fired from such a cell, the command request's `anchor` is that cell's address, and its text and selection are empty (not the prompt's).

BuiltinAction.description: One of the driver's built-in actions (e.g. coquille's submit, next...).

SpawnRequest.description: Start another driver (a shell), at the address `to` (one segment, e.g. `["$d1"]`): its messages come with their addresses under it, and messages to addresses under it go to it. For the host running the drivers, not for a driver: it starts `command`, in the terminal's working directory.

stream.description: Stream the text is delivered on (keyboard input from the interface).

text.description: Raw input text, as produced by the terminal emulator.

data.description: Arbitrary JSON relayed from the interface (a GUI cell message, a `proc://` request, an exec response, ...).

pixel.description: The cell's content area, in CSS pixels.

pty.description: The terminal grid, in character cells, when the cell holds a pty.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the content wanted, lowercase hex.

LibraryFetchRequest.description: Ask a library's authority (the driver that declared it, see `library`) for the content of one of its files, by hash. Sent by the host, addressed to the driver itself (`["$proc"]`); answered by a `library_content` carrying the same `request_id`.
